$comment: Issue #1460 — the classification vocabulary for multi-agent work.
JSON, not YAML, deliberately: labels-sync.yml reads this with plain `node -e`, and the
alternative was either a marketplace action (a supply-chain dependency for label names) or
adding js-yaml to a workflow that must not touch the root lockfile (spec 075).
THERE ARE DELIBERATELY NO `status:*` LABELS HERE. An issue's state is already first-class
GitHub data with exactly one copy: its assignee, its open/closed state, its sub-issue links,
and the PR that closes it. A status label would be a SECOND copy of that, and a second copy
drifts — an agent that sets `status:in-progress` and stops leaves an issue that reads as
actively worked forever, with nothing able to notice. Every label below classifies something
the repository has no other record of; none of them restates one it does.

labels.name: size:xs
labels.description: T-shirt size XS — under an hour. Maps to the Effort field: Low.

labels.name: size:s
labels.description: T-shirt size S — a few hours, one surface. Maps to the Effort field: Low.

labels.name: size:m
labels.description: T-shirt size M — a day or two, or more than one surface. Effort: Medium.

labels.name: size:l
labels.description: T-shirt size L — multi-day, needs a spec. Effort: High.

labels.name: size:xl
labels.description: T-shirt size XL — too big to deliver as one issue; split it into sub-issues. Effort: High.

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Stopped on something outside this issue. The blocker is named in a comment.

labels.name: spec-reservation
labels.description: PR that only claims a spec number on staging. Review for the number, not the design.
